newsitem.title: USA: Russia's Dubinin says rouble moves with market.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin says rouble moves with market.

text.p: The rouble's recent performance against the U.S. dollar has been market driven, Russian Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Saturday.
He added that Russia's central bank had bought dollars in recent days.
The Russian central bank spent $1.6 billion in August to support the rouble after a quicker than usual decline in the rouble's value made short-term Russian Treasury bills unattractive.
"In the last days of this month, we are buying dollars. It is a market fluctuation, nothing else," he told reporters after a meeting with G7 central bankers and finance ministers.
Dubinin said the recent health problems of President Boris Yeltsin, who is awaiting heart surgery, had not created a crisis for Russia's economy.
Some Western economists have suggested that political uncertainty, linked with Yeltsin's health, could be putting pressure on the rouble.
Dubinin has said Russia has sufficient reserves to keep the rouble within its crawling-peg exchange rate corridor.

Net reserves are one of the main economic indicators for which the International Monetary Fund, holding its annual meeting with the World Bank, sets monthly targets under its $10 billion, three-year loan agreement with Russia.
The central bank sets daily exchange rate corridors for the rouble, designed to allow a gradual depreciation of the rouble and put it in a range of 5,500-6,100 to the dollar on December 31.
Policy after that date is unclear but the draft 1997 budget assumes an average exchange rate of 5,560 roubles to the dollar. The rouble was bid at 5,397 per dollar late on Friday.
